Hard boundary checks performed:

- Centralizer formula: \(c_k=0\) contributes \(1\), fixed points contribute \(c_1!\), the identity gives \(n!\), and \(S_0\) gives the empty product \(1\).
- Splitting lemma: \(5\)-cycles in \(A_5\) have centralizer of order \(5\), entirely even, so \(24\to12+12\); \(3\)-cycles have centralizer of order \(6\) containing the odd transposition of the two fixed points, so the class remains size \(20\); double transpositions in \(A_4\) have centralizer order \(8\) containing odd elements and remain one class of size \(3\).
- The repaired coset algebra is valid: from \(c=h^{-1}t\) and \(cx=xc\), multiplication gives \(txt^{-1}=hxh^{-1}\), with \(h\) chosen after the arbitrary outside element \(c\).
- The extremal normal-subgroup proof exhausts: immediate \(3\)-cycle; a cycle of length at least \(4\); a \(3\)-cycle with further motion; or an even number of transpositions. The \(n\ge5\) hypothesis is used to obtain a fixed fifth point when exactly two transpositions occur. \(V_4\trianglelefteq A_4\) confirms the excluded \(n=4\) case is false.
- \(A_n\) generation was checked at \(n=3,4\); the derived-subgroup claims were checked at \(n=2\) and against the failing small-\(n\) alternating cases.
- The false-statement witnesses are genuine: \((123)\) and \((132)\) are in different \(A_4\)-classes; \(V_4\) is proper normal in \(A_4\); and \(\langle(1234),(13)\rangle\) preserves the two-block system and has order \(8\).
